question.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+1+4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{3}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
